newsitem.title: UK: UK insurance industry names genetic adviser.
newsitem.headline: UK insurance industry names genetic adviser.

text.p: The Association of British Insurers (ABI) said on Tuesday it has appointed Professor Sandy Raeburn as its part-time genetic adviser.
Raeburn is a genetecist based at the University of Nottingham, central England. He will assist in drawing up a code of practice for the handling of genetic information, the ABI said in a statement.

Medical advances in the field of genetics have led to concern among some consumer representatives, who fear that people at risk of some inherited diseases may be refused insurance or face higher premiums.

ABI director general Mark Boleat said, "We intend to have arrangements in place which demonstrate to everyone that there is no need for concern at the way in which information is used by insurance companies."
"(Raeburn) will ensure that insurance companies know the implications of any genetic data which may be passed to them," the ABI said.

"The Association has a long standing policy that members will not ask any individual to take genetic tests as a condition of receiving insurance. We take this opportunity to reaffirm this important policy," it added.
The ABI represents almost all UK insurers.
The UK government is in the process of setting up a Human Genetics Advisory Commission, but a spokeswoman told Reuters that an announcement on the identity of its members is unlikely before November.
The Commission will probably have 10 to 15 members, the Department of Trade and Industry spokeswoman said.
